contract: A connection cannot be assigned to a different tenant until its asynchronous session reset has acknowledged. Query execution uses the physical connection session tenant, not the caller label. A completed lease has no further right to query. The pool holds one physical connection.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: Tenant A releases the only connection and starts reset, but the reset callback has not run. Publishing the connection as idle allows tenant B to acquire it. Binding B is queued after reset while a synchronous query executes with session A. Keeping the connection unavailable until reset acknowledgement denies that query window.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: After reset acknowledgement B binds and queries B; an active A lease blocks other acquisition; repeated release is inert; failed reset destroys the connection instead of publishing it.
The session binding contract: are queries scoped by the physical session tenant, or does the database enforce an independent per-query tenant envelope?

Under this contract: A connection cannot be assigned to a different tenant until its asynchronous session reset has acknowledged. Query execution uses the physical connection session tenant, not the caller label. A completed lease has no further right to query. The pool holds one physical connection. the traced behavior is a defect. Alternative: If the database independently scopes each query by the caller envelope and ignores residual session tenant for access, early reuse does not cross the tenant boundary under that alternative contract; the physical reset trace alone cannot establish data exposure.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
